files.purpose: New at B3 (status A, 304 lines, added by commit d70cff8fe 'refactor: audit cleanups'): the single AppKit press-tracking strip that now backs every drag handle in the app, replacing three separate B2 NSView classes (SidebarResizeHandleView at B2 WindowChrome.swift:402-571, TerminalResizeHandleView at B2 TerminalPanel.swift:142-256, PanelDragHandleView at B2 SubagentPanel.swift:677-738). DragHandleView (lines 6-267) owns the cursor rect, first-click acceptance, the no-window-move press, an optional slop before a press becomes a drag, a pushed drag cursor, an optional double-click callback, travel reporting per Axis (horizontal x only, vertical y positive up, free with y running down like a panel offset) and, when a Grip is configured, a centred CALayer grip bar that grows on hover plus an optional glow layer below it, both painted in NSColor.labelColor. DragHandle (lines 270-304) is the NSViewRepresentable face that pushes one configuration (axis, grip, cursor, dragCursor, slop, isActive, four callbacks) into the view on make and on every update; its three B3 call sites are SidebarResizeHandle (WindowChrome.swift:379-400: horizontal, Grip 10/22/2.5, glowInset 30, refreshesHoverOnLayout, .columnResize), TerminalResizeHandle (TerminalPanel.swift:114-131: vertical, Grip 12/28/2.5, .resizeUpDown) and PanelDragHandle (SubagentPanel.swift:646-666: free, slop 2, open-hand cursor, closed-hand drag cursor, optional double-click).

func makeNSView(context:) -> DragHandleView (282-286); func updateNSView(_:context:) (288-290); private func apply(to:) (292-303)
calls_into: NSCursor.push() on the drag cursor (215) and NSCursor.pop() (132, 226)
Chrome constants only at call sites: SidebarResizeHandle passes Chrome.trafficLightTop + Chrome.trafficLightDiameter as glowInset (WindowChrome.swift:391)
state_owned: pressOrigin: NSPoint, the press location in window coordinates (63, 199)
trackingArea: NSTrackingArea?, present only while a grip is configured (64, 234-245)
hasConfigured: Bool, so the first configure(grip:) snaps the grip once and later re-renders never snap a running hover animation (65, 110-113)
isHovering: Bool, set by enter/exit and re-read from the real cursor by refreshHover (66, 144-151)
isDragging: Bool, true from the press when slop == 0, otherwise from the first move past the slop (67, 205, 214)
gripLayer and glowLayer CALayers, glow added first so the grip draws on top (68-69, 87-88)
configuration mirrored from the SwiftUI side: axis, grip, cursor, dragCursor, slop, isActive and the four callbacks (32-56, 292-303)
side_effects: Pushes the drag cursor onto NSCursor's stack when a slop-gated drag starts (215) and pops it on release (226) or when the view leaves its window mid-drag (130-133)
Invalidates the window's cursor rects when the cursor object changes identity or isActive flips (42, 52)
Adds or removes an NSTrackingArea when a grip is configured or dropped (108, 234-245)
Mutates CALayer frames, corner radius and opacity inside a CATransaction, animated 0.18 s ease-out or with actions disabled (153-181)
platform_assumptions: AppKit window coordinates have y running up; .vertical reports point.y - pressOrigin.y (positive upward, the direction the terminal drawer grows) and .free inverts it to pressOrigin.y - point.y so y runs down like a panel offset (257-265)
Only a cursor rect shows the cursor before a press, and the first click must work when the window is not key (doc comment 4-5, acceptsFirstMouse 183)
mouseDownCanMoveWindow false: the press never moves the window, even where a strip overlaps the title bar (185-186)
No mouseExited arrives while the button is held, so the release re-reads the cursor place (229-231; the comment states the author's reliance, not independently verified)
NSTrackingArea .activeAlways + .inVisibleRect: hover is tracked whether or not the app is frontmost and follows the visible rect (242)
hitTest returning nil makes an inactive strip transparent to clicks (194-196)
NSCursor push/pop is a global stack, so an unbalanced push would leak a cursor; the view pops on removal from the window mid-drag (129-133)
ui_elements: Grip bar (gripLayer): rounded, cornerRadius thickness/2, centred in the strip; a vertical bar thickness x length for .horizontal, a horizontal bar length x thickness otherwise; length restLength at rest and shownLength when isActive && (hovering || dragging); opacity grip.alpha (default 0.6) when shown, 0 otherwise; colour NSColor.labelColor resolved in the effective appearance (153-181)

Glow panel (glowLayer): cornerRadius 4, frame x = bounds.minX + 0.5, y = glowInset, width max(0, bounds.width - 1), height max(0, bounds.height - glowInset); opacity dragGlow (0.10) while dragging, hoverGlow (0.05) while hovered, 0 otherwise; only when grip.glowInset is set (174-179)
Cursor rect over the whole bounds with the configured cursor, only while isActive (188-192); optional drag cursor pushed while held (46, 215)
No visible element when grip is nil (the panel drag handles): both layers stay at opacity 0 (154-157)
feature_notes: SOURCE FACT: the file is new at B3; git diff B2..B3 shows 304 insertions and the only commit touching it is d70cff8fe ('refactor: audit cleanups'), which in the same change reduced SidebarResizeHandle (WindowChrome.swift), TerminalResizeHandle (TerminalPanel.swift) and PanelDragHandle (SubagentPanel.swift) from NSViewRepresentable wrappers over their own NSView classes to SwiftUI Views whose body is a configured DragHandle (B3 WindowChrome.swift:379-400, TerminalPanel.swift:114-131, SubagentPanel.swift:646-666).

SOURCE FACT (sidebar strip, B2 WindowChrome.swift:402-571 vs B3): the configuration reproduces B2 exactly (rest 10, shown 22, thickness 2.5, alpha 0.6, glow 0.05/0.10, glow radius 4, glow inset trafficLightTop + trafficLightDiameter, 0.18 s ease-out, hover re-read on every layout, .columnResize, isActive gating of cursor rect, hover and hitTest). The only differences: mouseUp is now ignored unless a drag is in progress (222-223), a strip removed from its window mid-drag now clears isDragging (130-131), and mouseDown checks clickCount == 2 for an onDoubleClick the sidebar never sets. None is observable in normal use.

SOURCE FACT (terminal strip, B2 TerminalPanel.swift:142-256 vs B3): the grip literals are unchanged (rest 12, shown 28, thickness 2.5, alpha 0.6, 0.18 s ease-out, .resizeUpDown, travel positive upward). Two behaviours are new for the terminal strip: on release it re-reads the real cursor position before animating the grip (230-231), so a drag released off the strip now retracts the grip, where B2 left isHovering at the last enter/exit value; and on entering a window it re-reads hover and snaps the grip (134-137), which B2's terminal view did not override. The grip update at release now runs after onEnd instead of before it (B2: onChange, isDragging = false, updateGrip, onEnd; B3: isDragging = false, onChange, onEnd, refreshHover, updateGrip). The terminal strip also gains an invisible glow layer (glowInset nil, opacity always 0) and an isActive that is always true.

SOURCE FACT (panel drag handles, B2 SubagentPanel.swift:677-738 vs B3): no observable change. slop 2, open-hand cursor, closed-hand drag cursor pushed once the travel passes the slop on either axis, double-click on clickCount 2, y-down travel, pop on release and on removal mid-drag are all kept. The view is now layer-backed with two invisible layers and runs updateGrip/refreshHover with no grip, which draws nothing.

SOURCE FACT: the mouseDownCanMoveWindow comment was generalised from the sidebar-specific B2 text about the strip running through the title bar to 'The drag owns the press, so the window never moves with it.' (185); the behaviour is identical.

SOURCE FACT, latent only: with slop == 0 mouseDown sets isDragging without pushing dragCursor (205-207), yet mouseUp and viewDidMoveToWindow pop whenever dragCursor != nil (132, 226). No B3 call site combines slop 0 with a drag cursor (sidebar and terminal pass no dragCursor; the panel handle passes slop 2), so no unbalanced pop is reachable.

SOURCE FACT: onChange is called with the release travel before onEnd, and onEnd is not called when the view is taken out of its window mid-drag (only isDragging is cleared and the cursor popped, 129-133).
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: the comment at 229 says no exit arrives while the button is held; the port's hover-at-release behaviour for the terminal strip depends on it, and whether Avalonia raises PointerExited while the pointer is captured on Windows has to be established by a test, not assumed.
